idea-plugin.name: Mermaid Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Syntax highlighting and real validation for .mmd/.mermaid diagram source files (flowchart, sequence, and class diagrams): a real paid competitor's reviewers reported it "shows false warnings for valid non-ASCII subgraph identifiers" and "false errors for valid node shapes where the node contains non-ASCII characters" -- this plugin's lexer is Unicode-aware throughout (no ASCII-only character-class check anywhere in the identifier/label path), so those exact false positives structurally cannot happen here.

Unterminated string literals, unmatched/mismatched node-shape brackets, and `subgraph` blocks missing their `end` are flagged as real errors -- exactly the "does it actually validate my syntax" gap the cited 1-star review described.

A "Preview" tab renders the diagram visually via the real mermaid.js (bundled), next to the text editor -- the direct fix for that same review ("It opens and shows me a bunch of icons on page. That's it. No other functionality at all."). The preview zooms and pans (Ctrl+mouse wheel or pinch to zoom, drag or scroll to pan, fit and 100% buttons), switches diagram theme independently of the editor theme (a light, printable diagram in a dark IDE), and exports the diagram as SVG or PNG. If this IDE build doesn't support embedded browser rendering, the tab shows a plain message instead; everything else in the plugin is unaffected.

Works alongside JetBrains's own Mermaid plugin (bundled with IntelliJ IDEA from 2026.2): when both are installed, you're asked once which editor should own .mmd/.mermaid files, and the Preview tab stays available with either one.

Mermaid Companion Pro is an optional paid tier; everything described above stays free. Export on Save keeps a diagram's SVG and/or PNG export up to date every time you save the file, written next to it. A diagram that doesn't render leaves the existing exports untouched, and an unchanged diagram leaves the files alone.
